identity_bindings.input_title: Clustered Interval Calibration And Synthetic Segmentation Robustness

rubric.instructions: Review the rendered pixels from one normal research-presentations production invocation. Check that each page contains source-specific content from the supplied engineering bundle rather than placeholders; exact CUHK Beamer identity is visible; the main scientific object is prominent and projection-readable; math, native plots, and medical images are semantically correct where present; no internal RRL/GSC/SRC, QA, provenance, workflow, repo path, run ID, or implementation language leaks into audience-facing slides; repeated generic cards or one-template pages are rejected; and the deck reads as one coherent research update rather than disconnected benchmark pages. For multi-workstream bundles, confirm that each workstream stays internally continuous and that any independent workstream transition is visible without inventing a causal relation. Separately review the deck_contact_sheet item as a deck-level rhythm object: adjacent-page density jumps, repeated composition face, overfull or empty pages, redundant summary filler, result -> failure -> next-experiment rhythm, workstream transition balance, and title/object/formula/image alternation must meet a mature doctoral group-meeting or strong conference-talk bar. The top-level package PASS is not enough; provide item-level judgement and observations for deck_contact_sheet. Do not infer visual quality from filenames or hashes.
source_contracts: The engineering regression bundle is public-safe and explicitly excluded from Stage 5 holdouts.
Stage 2 gold/reference pixels are used only for compatible composition selection.
The deck-quality loop may repair at most once and must fail closed/no-winner for unsafe findings or unresolved blockers.

observations: CUHK crest, purple header, section navigation, and slide number are visibly rendered.
The mixed-model equation and ICC definition are clean and readable.
The page is substantially empty below and around the equation; it reads as an underdeveloped formula page rather than a complete research-update slide.
No visible RRL/GSC/SRC, QA, repository, run-ID, or implementation-language text appears on this page.
item_reviews.summary: Readable model content and identity are present, but the page needs a substantive supporting visual or explanation to avoid an empty one-object composition.

observations: A prominent three-panel coverage-versus-ICC plot is visible, with distinct G=8, G=20, and G=50 conditions, method key, nominal-coverage reference, and data-source note.
The plotted red and teal trajectories support the stated claim that cluster-robust intervals recover coverage as ICC increases.
The plot, annotations, and two supporting interpretations are readable and visually balanced.
CUHK visual identity remains consistent and no internal workflow or provenance language is visible.
item_reviews.summary: A coherent, source-specific results page centered on a readable native plot.

observations: The page uses a connected DGP stress grid → center hierarchy → interval procedures → endpoints schematic rather than a generic card layout.
Visible labels specify centers, ICC levels, balanced/imbalanced clusters, 400 repetitions per cell, interval choices, and coverage/width/bias endpoints.
Connector direction and the explanatory footer make the experimental sequence legible.
No visible internal process, QA, repo, run-ID, or implementation-language leak appears.
item_reviews.summary: A visually coherent and specific simulation-design diagram that continues the clustered-interval workstream.

observations: The slide visibly presents the negative result with labeled G=8 coverage bars across ICC values, uncertainty bars, a 0.95 target line, and an annotation identifying continued below-nominal coverage.
The adjacent text explains the failure condition and names the proposed next tests, making the failure interpretable rather than decorative.
The bar chart is the dominant scientific object and remains readable at page scale.
No internal workflow/provenance text is visible.
item_reviews.summary: A strong failure-analysis slide with a clear visual diagnosis and direct transition toward follow-up testing.

observations: The slide explicitly connects failure evidence to sampling manipulations, comparator arms, and a go/no-go decision rule.
The flow diagram visibly carries forward G=8, ICC=.5, imbalanced clusters, CR2 small-sample correction, wild-cluster bootstrap, and the coverage threshold.
Its structure provides a clear next-experiment continuation of the preceding negative-result slide.
No visible RRL/GSC/SRC, QA, provenance, repo-path, run-ID, or implementation-language text appears.
item_reviews.summary: A specific and continuous next-experiment plan that follows directly from the documented failure.

observations: The page visibly marks a “Workstream transition” and states that segmentation robustness is an independent workstream with no causal bridge asserted.
Input, ground truth, prediction, and TP/FP/FN error panels show the same ring-like case; the ROI box and arrow link the error image to matching zoom crops.
The color legend is adjacent to the images and makes TP, FP, and FN semantics interpretable.
The medical-image comparison is clearly distinct from the interval-calibration workstream while retaining the deck identity.
item_reviews.summary: A semantically clear same-case segmentation comparison with an explicit, appropriately non-causal workstream transition.

observations: The seven-page sequence visibly establishes a coherent clustered-interval arc: model, coverage result, design, failure, and next experiment; the segmentation page then visibly declares an independent workstream transition.
The deck alternates formula, multi-panel plot, process schematic, bar-chart failure evidence, experiment flow, and medical-image comparison, avoiding repeated generic card pages.
The rendered title page visibly leaks internal workflow/source-bundle phrasing: “One-call production regression from source bundle to exact CUHK deck.”
The statistical-model page is visibly much emptier than the neighboring pages and creates an abrupt low-density beat early in the deck.
The result → failure → next-experiment sequence is clear and effective; the independent segmentation transition is explicitly balanced rather than implying a causal link.
item_reviews.summary: The deck has strong visual continuity, identity, object alternation, and workstream handling, but it is blocked by title-slide workflow leakage and an underfilled model-page composition.

non_blocking_notes: CUHK identity is consistently visible through the crest, purple navigation bar, typography, and footer treatment.
The scientific pages use varied, content-appropriate compositions rather than repeated template cards.
The medical-image workstream is visually and verbally separated from the clustered-interval workstream without asserting an unsupported causal relationship.
